items.title: Stadium Boom Brings New Pressure to Deliver Beyond Game Day
items.summary: Speaking at Sportico's Invest New York event, Related Companies president Bruce Beal Jr. said it is a fallacy that building a stadium automatically improves everything around it. He and Pat Ryan Jr., who oversaw Northwestern's $870 million New Ryan Field, argued the new wave of venues, now measured in billions, must anchor neighbourhoods that work year-round with housing, restaurants and retail. Related is applying that thinking at Willets Point in Queens, where NYCFC's 25,000-seat Etihad Park opens in 2027 alongside 2,500 affordable apartments.
items.what_it_means: Billion-dollar venues now have to earn their return on the days without a game, not just on game day.

items.title: Q&A: Fire's Dan Moriarty talks career, marketing brand vs. team
items.summary: Chicago Fire CMO Dan Moriarty told Ad Age, in an interview summarised by SBJ, that the pandemic accelerated digital community building because teams had to keep fans and partners engaged without live events. He said game day used to be the be-all and end-all, and now the job is growing digital audiences and working out how to monetise them. Coming from Hyatt, he described sports marketing as the opposite of a planned brand launch, because one injury, bad result or trade can undo years of work.
items.what_it_means: Team marketers are shifting effort from game day to building and monetising digital audiences that hold up whatever the results.

items.title: KPMG: Sports content spending up 57% since 2021 among leading media platforms
items.summary: New KPMG data shows sports content investment across 13 leading media and platform companies, including YouTube, Comcast/NBCU, Disney, Amazon and Netflix, reached roughly $29B last year, up 57% since 2021 and about 14% of their $207B total content spend. User-generated content spend grew faster, up 75% in five years to around $46B. KPMG's Scott Purdy said the companies that build an ecosystem around their sports rights, from UGC and gaming to bundled subscriptions and retail, will get the most from the investment.
items.what_it_means: Platforms are putting a growing share of content budgets into sport, and the payoff depends on what they build around the rights.

items.title: When baseball disappears from the screen (even the small screen), fandom suffers
items.summary: In an SBJ op-ed, communications adviser Ryan Baldwin writes that his 11-year-old son came into baseball this year through YouTube, the MLB app and roster pages he checked daily. A reported MLB memo says active players' images and video would be removed from league and club sites during a lockout, as happened in 2021. Baldwin asks MLB to explain any removal on the page, keep names and statistics visible and link to both sides' bargaining proposals, so a new fan finds an explanation instead of a blank silhouette.
items.what_it_means: For new fans the official app and site are the front door to the sport, so what a league does there during a dispute shapes fandom.

items.title: Ticket Resellers StubHub, Vivid Seats Give Dismal Earnings Reports
items.summary: Vivid Seats and StubHub both missed third-quarter targets despite a strong sports calendar that included the end of the men's World Cup and the start of college football and the NFL. Vivid Seats' shares are down nearly 80% this year, leaving it worth under $17 million against almost $2 billion at its 2021 listing, while StubHub's market value has fallen to about $2.2 billion from an $8.6 billion IPO. The piece points to resale competition, debt, regulation and internal missteps, while Live Nation, which owns Ticketmaster, reported double-digit growth.
items.what_it_means: Investors are rewarding ticketing businesses tied to primary sales and punishing standalone resale marketplaces.

items.title: Inside Diljit Dosanjh's record-breaking Aura tour
items.summary: Diljit Dosanjh became the first South Asian artist to headline Wembley Stadium, selling it out within 48 hours, after 15 sold-out North American dates grossed $32m across 225,000 fans. Live Nation's Nidhish Varughese says the team used streaming data, past ticket sales and presale demand to choose markets, including ones not usually played by South Asian tours. What surprised him most was how far fans travelled, with smaller regions in the US and UK feeding into shows in Atlanta, Orlando, Birmingham, Manchester and London.
items.what_it_means: Streaming and presale data are helping promoters find audiences in markets that never looked viable, and those fans will travel.

items.title: NHL sponsor business booming as Global Series begins in Finland
items.summary: The NHL opens its Global Series in Helsinki with 75 corporate partners and a league-record 15 global sponsors, with Procter & Gamble and Michelob Ultra among the new additions. Michelob Ultra is the league's first official US beer sponsor since the Bud Light deal ended after 2021-22. Several partners did not return, including SkipTheDishes, though the league signed a broader deal with DoorDash covering national Wednesday games and playoffs on Prime Video in Canada.
items.what_it_means: The NHL's sponsor growth is coming from global deals that follow the league into international markets.

items.title: Fourteen sponsors activating across WTGL's debut season
items.summary: WTGL, the women's version of the TGL golf simulator league, launched last weekend with 14 sponsors activating at the SoFi Center in South Florida. Twelve of the 14 are existing TGL partners, including AT&T, Best Buy, Omega and SoFi. Topgolf and Go Rentals are new and will also activate around TGL when its season starts in late December.
items.what_it_means: Bundling a women's league with an established men's property gives it a full sponsor roster from day one.

items.title: What the NBA Thinks It Will Do Better Than EuroLeague
items.summary: NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum told Sportico's Invest New York event that European basketball lags other sports in revenue despite strong fan affinity, and existing teams are tired of investing without their franchise values rising. NBA Europe will enter markets EuroLeague does not serve, including the UK, with top franchise fees expected around $1 billion. Tatum pitched new arenas as an investment case, with 30 to 40 home nights of basketball and 320 other days to fill with concerts, conferences and events.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is selling Europe on arenas that earn year-round, with basketball as the anchor tenant.

items.title: Altitude+ growth accelerates with Comcast, local distribution
items.summary: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment's Altitude+ streaming service for the Avalanche and Nuggets has grown faster since Comcast and local broadcasters widened its distribution, according to a Denver Business Journal report summarised by SBJ. Annual subscriptions tripled during the season, registered users grew 63% and total views rose 186%. KSE credits features such as extra camera angles, pre- and post-game shows, live chat and a multi-game view.
items.what_it_means: Team-owned streaming grows fastest when it is widely distributed and offers fans more than the game feed.
